messages.message: Google Scholar stems words; openproceedings matches them exactly, so `trust` matches only those forms (not plurals or other endings). Add `$` or `*` where they should count (e.g. `trust$`).

`model$`: `$` has no documented wildcard meaning in Google Scholar; openproceedings reads it as the Web of Science zero-or-one wildcard, so it matches `model` plus at most one character (e.g. a plural), and results for it may differ from the Scholar run.
`large language model` is read as the phrase `"large language model"` (openproceedings decision-002); Google Scholar itself would have ORed only the neighbouring words.
`source:PMLR` is read as `venue:ICML`.
`source:` is Google Scholar syntax — write `venue:NeurIPS`, `venue:ICLR` or `venue:ICML` (Scholar-mode input translates it automatically).
`venue:(…)` takes values joined by OR, e.g. `venue:(ICLR OR ICML)`.
`2026..2020` runs backwards — write `2020..2026`.
`author:` is not a field — use one of `title:`, `abstract:`, `venue:`, `year:`, `track:`, `status:`, `source:`, or quote the text to search for it.
`poster` is not a track (values take no wildcards or quotes) — use one of `main`, `datasets_benchmarks`, `position`, `workshop`, `competition`, `tiny_papers`, `blogpost`, `other`, `unknown`.
`20x` is not a year — `year:` takes a four-digit year or an inclusive range, e.g. `year:2024` or `year:2020..2026`.
Every part of this query is negated (`NOT …`), so it would match almost everything — add something to search for, e.g. `trust NOT bias`.
`-`: to exclude a word, put one `-` straight before it after a space (`trust -bias`); to search a hyphenated term, quote it.

The quote `"` is followed directly by a letter or digit, so it is unclear whether it opens or closes a phrase — put a space between them, or drop the inner quotes (a phrase cannot contain the same kind of quote).
`NEAR/x` needs a whole-number distance up to 100 — write e.g. `NEAR/3` (at most 3 words apart).
Empty parentheses `()` — remove them or put a term inside.
`~` has no letters or digits, so it can't match anything — remove it (to exclude a word, write `-word` with no space).
`OR` needs a word, phrase or group after it — add one, or remove `OR`.
`abstract:` can't be used inside `title:(…)`: a term is searched in one field — move it out of the group.
`model(`: a parenthesis touching a word would be read as AND (`model(s)` means `model AND s`) — for a plural write `model$`, for a group put a space: `model (s)`.
`: model` starts with a colon, so no field is named — a field name must touch its colon, e.g. `title:trust`.
The query nests groups or `NOT`s more than 64 deep here — remove a level of parentheses or a `NOT`.
The query is 2,001 characters long; the limit is 2,000 — shorten it, e.g. replace a list of word forms with one wildcard.
`(trust OR reliance` has no closing parenthesis — add `)` where the group ends.
The phrase starting `"large language` has no closing quote — add a closing `"`.
The `*` in `abcd.*` follows `.`, not a letter or digit, so it would match any word starting `abcd` — put it straight after the stem, e.g. `abcd*`.
`tr*st` has a `*` that is neither a wildcard at the end of a word (e.g. `bench*`, `model$`) nor closed LaTeX math (`$x$`) — search the whole word, or close the math.
`大语言模型`: Chinese, Japanese and Korean text is not split into words, so this matches only the exact run — `大语言模型*` also finds longer runs that start with it.
`PMLR` is searched as text in any paper, not as a source — to OR it into the filter, write `source:(… OR PMLR)`.
`−bias` starts with `−`, which is not an operator, so the word is searched — to exclude it, type an ASCII hyphen: `-bias`.
`‘AI’` starts with a single quote, which does not make a phrase — use double quotes: `"…"`.
`or` is searched as a word — write `OR` to combine terms (operators are uppercase only).
AND binds tighter than OR, so this is read as `(trust AND LLM) OR agent` — add parentheses if you meant something else.
This `track:` clause is nested, so the default track filter still applies to the whole query — add a top-level `track:` clause to override it.
`PMLR` also hosts other venues; only ICML is indexed, so it matches ICML papers only.
`alpha` finds the word only: abstracts' `$\alpha$` and `α` are indexed as `α`, so search `alpha OR α`.
`C++` is searched as `c`: symbols such as `+`, `#` and `.` are not indexed, so it matches every `c`.
The wildcard `be*` keeps fewer than 3 letters or digits before `*`, so it would match too many words — use a longer stem (e.g. `bench*`, not `be*`).
`tru*` expands to 201 terms (more than 200) — use a longer stem.
